the depressor and powerful sympathoinhibitor evoked from the midline medulla are mediated by GABAergic inhibition of sympathoactivating neurons in the rostrally located VLM, whereas the sympathoinhibitor is also mediated by sympathoexcitators in the caudally located VLM.
the depressor and powerful sympathoinhibitor that can be evoced from the caudalis medulla is mediated, at least in part, by GABAergic inhibition of sympathoexctitatory neurons in rostral VML.

the depressor and renal sympathoinhibitory responses evoked by glutamatergic stimulation of the caudal medullary depressor area are mediated by GABAergic inhibition of sympatho- and vasomotor neurons in the rostroventrolateral medulla.

the neural circuitry of cardiovascular regulation.
the neural circuitry in the medulla that mediates the depressor and vasodepressor response to stimulation of neurons in and around the caudal nucleus of the solitary tract.
the role of GABA in the control of blood pressure and sympathetic nerve activity.

the caudal medullary depressor and sympathoexcitability responses are mediated by GABAergic synapses located in the rostral ventral medulla.
